discussion_comments.comment_body:
With this code, if the argument is blank, like the following, it will throw a type error:

```ts
const ref = useRef<HTMLDivElement>()
```

So you have to change the overload to this, don't you?:

```ts
export function useRef<T>(initialValue: T): RefObject<T>
export function useRef<T>(initialValue: T | null): RefObject<T | null>
export function useRef<T = undefined>(): RefObject<T | undefined>
```
There may be some discussion about updating the test, but if we accept this PR, the old test is wrong. The value of `c.req.param('id')` can be `string | undefined`.

I put out a PR related to this.

https://github.com/exoego/hono/pull/5

discussion_comments.comment_body:
> is this really needed?
> 
> since we already provide a check for this
> 
> ```ts
> const headerName = options?.headerName ?? 'X-Request-Id'
> ```


I haven't documented this yet, but it is for internal use only. For example, logging.
Specifying empty string means that the user expects no request ID to be present in  request/response.
And we need to check for empty string.

```ts
console.log("" ?? "string") // empty
console.log("" || "string") // string
console.log("" ? "A" : "B") // B
```

discussion_comments.comment_body:
It simplifies code in my opinion.

It allows
```javascript
event.multiValueHeaders?.['host']?.[0]
```
instead of
```javascript
'multiValueHeaders' in event
      ? event.multiValueHeaders.['host']?.[0]
      : undefined
```

and it also allows
```javascript
} else if (event.multiValueHeaders) {
  for (const [k, values] of
    Object.entries(event.multiValueHeaders)) {
```
instead of 
```javascript
 } else if ('multiValueHeaders' in event) {
  for (const [k, values] of
    Object.entries(event.multiValueHeaders || {})) {
```

I tried it, but `event.requestContext.http?.httpMethod` is `undefined`. So, `method` must be:

```ts
const method = 'httpMethod' in event ? event.httpMethod : event.requestContext.http.method
```
I think the previous code is fine. We just need to make the type for when it's undefined be `string | undefined` or `string | null`.
